edits.text:
# Misofish

A small, independently written MiroFish-inspired scenario lab: **context → fictional people → streamed conversations → final synthesis**. One shared isometric room has an extruded floor/walls, upright depth-sorted human figures, wandering, and speaker-anchored speech bubbles. A plain transcript remains available.

**Hard limit: 10 simulation agents.** Default: 10 agents, 3 rounds. One active simulation per server/data directory; four concurrent model calls maximum. The preparer and report are ordinary SDK requests, not additional autonomous agents.

## Run locally (macOS/Linux)

Python 3.11+ required. No Node build, Zep account, agent framework, containers or database server.

```sh
cd /Users/nayira.venu/Documents/PEP/misofish
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.lock
# Set OPENAI_API_KEY directly in your terminal using your normal secret manager.
# Never paste the key into chat, browser inputs, or committed files.
export OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini   # optional; this is the default
.venv/bin/python -m misofish.server
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:8000**. The server also opens without a key so you can inspect the UI and saved runs; preparing/running stays disabled until `OPENAI_API_KEY` is present. Direct Python startup reads environment variables only. `run.sh` explicitly loads this project's trusted local `.env`, then starts the same server. `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is honored by the SDK; your endpoint must support Responses API structured outputs.

### Configured GPT-5.4 mini (Azure)

The authorized Azure key and lightweight deployment were copied from `../manta-code/.env` into this project's ignored `.env` with owner-only permissions. Only `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` (Azure `/openai/v1/`) and `OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini` were copied; MANTA and its other credentials were untouched. The Azure v1 API uses the existing `OpenAI` client and does not need MANTA's legacy API-version setting.

```sh
./run.sh --port 8765
```

Keep `.env` private; it is trusted shell configuration, not user input. Never paste or commit its contents. Changes to MANTA's key are not synchronized automatically. GPT-5.4 mini was verified with a live structured connectivity check and one fictional persona request. The user subsequently completed a ten-agent, three-round election run; its saved actions and report remain readable. The upgraded streaming/scheduling pipeline was verified against a real-SDK localhost SSE fixture, not another paid simulation.

If port 8000 is occupied, add `--port 8765`. Stop the existing Misofish preview with Ctrl+C before restarting it with your environment configured; do not stop unrelated services.

1. Write a scenario; optionally paste/import UTF-8 TXT or Markdown background.
2. Choose 1–10 agents and 1–10 rounds. Accept the data-sharing notice and prepare personas.
3. Review their perspectives; explicitly start the discussion.
4. Watch the **Conversation room**: no preassigned partners or pair cards. Free people wander; proximity-weighted chance selects encounters at runtime. They approach before talking and separate afterwards. Different encounters overlap; replies wait for completed arguments. Select a person/bubble for their full speech and perspective, or **Transcript** for numbered turns. **Pause visual motion** freezes animation without cancelling generation.
5. Read **Final synthesis**: a prominent bottom line, development of the discussion, agreements, disagreements, unresolved questions and evidence links. This view opens as synthesis generation begins; a summary preview also appears near the status panel.
6. Export a Markdown report including every numbered turn. Saved experiments survive restarts. **Replay saved conversation** is recorded playback, not live model generation.

**Real streaming:** the official SDK emits model text deltas through a durable local Server-Sent Events journal. Speech bubbles and synthesis show actual partial text, not delayed typing animation or raw JSON. Drafts are marked **LIVE DRAFT** and cannot be reply targets or cited evidence. Completed turns are validated and checkpointed immediately. Reconnecting replays event IDs without repeating model calls; finished snapshots remain authoritative.

Cancel closes in-flight streams when cancellation is observed; an unresponsive transport can still wait until its timeout. Finished turns—including partial-round progress—remain saved; unvalidated drafts are discarded. No new dependent reply, round or report starts after cancellation. Failed or interrupted runs never resume automatically. Ctrl+C asks the worker to stop and waits for pending requests. Requests have a 60-second timeout and no SDK retries.

## Why this is smaller

| Reference architecture (source-observed) | Misofish design |
| --- | --- |
| Ontology + Zep Cloud graph ingestion | Bounded source text supplied directly |
| Graph entities → separate platform profile files | One structured persona response; application-assigned IDs |
| Twitter/Reddit OASIS/CAMEL environments | Runtime spatial encounters in one shared room/transcript |
| Child processes, file IPC, cloud-memory finalization | One worker thread; SQLite checkpoints |
| Tool-driven report agent | One structured report call, checked citation IDs |
| Vue/Vite frontend + Flask services | Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS + loopback stdlib HTTP server |

The choice is optimized **for a ten-persona local experiment**, not feature parity or proven forecast quality. The backend owns persistent room positions and chooses encounters from currently available nearby people at runtime—no precomputed pair list or permanent pairing. Participants reserve only their exchange; other people wander. Up to four encounters/SDK calls overlap; dependent replies receive only finalized arguments. Movement/contact selection is a bounded stochastic heuristic, not LLM-controlled navigation or a crowd/obstacle solver. No extra model calls/dependencies or speed/cost benchmark claims.

### Bounds and costs

- Scenario: 1–2,000 characters. Source: at most 20,000 characters; over-limit content is rejected, never silently truncated.
- Exactly the requested 1–10 personas; generated count checked before anything runs. Stored roster and config revalidated at start and each round.
- Every persona decides once per round: `post`, `reply`, or `pass`, plus a categorical stance. Dependent replies must address their completed partner argument; other reply targets must be visible, completed, non-pass turns from another person.
- A round is a turn-budget cycle, not assigned seating. Each person speaks once per cycle to preserve the cost cap; an unpaired available person may make a solo observation. Finished people can wander before their next cycle. Old saved runs have a display-only room layout because they contain no historical spatial positions.
- Last 20 prior-round actions, each persona's own last action and the direct partner turn are provided to decisions. Full finalized history goes to the final synthesis. One-person and odd-numbered casts are supported without adding participants.
- Up to `2 + agents × rounds` logical calls: **32 by default, 102 at maximum**. SDK retry budget is zero; output ceilings are 3,000 tokens for preparation, 4,000 for synthesis and 700 per spoken turn. GPT-5 calls explicitly use `reasoning.effort=none` so short speech budgets are not spent on hidden reasoning. Reported completed-call token totals are shown; interrupted calls can incur additional provider charges not reflected in those totals.
- Finalized turns persist even if another stream fails. A round counts as completed only when its entire cast finishes. Safe errors and partial progress remain visible; failed drafts are never invented into successful evidence.

## Security and limits

This is a **single-user local development tool**, not a production server. It binds only `127.0.0.1`, allowlists Host and static assets, blocks cross-origin mutations, requires JSON, caps request size, parameterizes SQL and renders model/input text without `innerHTML`. A process lock prevents multiple live servers from sharing the same data directory. Local processes/users are trusted; there is no login, encryption or multi-tenant isolation. Do not expose it via a tunnel or reverse proxy.

Credentials stay in the server environment, never prompts or browser/storage. Scenario/source, persona context, and simulated actions **leave your machine for the configured OpenAI endpoint** when you prepare/start. Responses request `store=False`; that is not a guarantee of zero provider retention. Review provider privacy policies before supplying sensitive data. SQLite records under `data/runs.db` are plaintext, persist until you remove them, and can be removed manually after stopping the server. Use fictional/non-sensitive input.

No PDFs/OCR, social-network ranking, live interviews, audio, heavy 3D engine, forecast calibration, population sampling or external tools. The local illustrated figures are fictional representations, not real people's likenesses. Spoken arguments and synthesis are observable outputs—not hidden chain-of-thought. Citation validation proves a turn exists and isn't a pass; **you must verify that it supports the claim**. Different model calls can disagree or invent interpretations. Results are synthetic possibilities, not probabilities or factual forecasts.

## Verify without paid calls

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
.venv/bin/python -m pip check
# Optional JavaScript syntax check if Node is already installed:
node --check web/app.js
node --check web/room.js
```

Tests use temporary SQLite stores and a localhost-only SSE fixture for the **real OpenAI SDK**. They cover cap bypasses, parallel lanes, sequential parent visibility, decoded partial text, failures/refusal, citations, per-turn persistence, cancellation, event cursor replay/recovery, HTTP guards and exports. The fixture isn't an application demo mode; production always uses the configured SDK provider.

Initial build verification: **20 tests passed**, real-browser ten-persona/two-round workflow passed against the localhost SDK fixture, and responsive overflow checks passed at 375/768/1024/1440px. Model setup verification: **22 tests passed**, plus two small live Azure GPT-5.4 mini requests (connectivity and one fictional persona). No predictive evaluation, performance benchmark, or dependency vulnerability audit was performed.

Conversation upgrade: **35 tests passed**. Browser render samples observed two parallel live lanes, partial human text before any finalized turn, eight unique completed turns, recorded replay and citation navigation. Existing election run opened directly in Final synthesis with all ten figures/thirty actions preserved. No overflow at 375/768/1024/1440px; reduced-motion removes figure animation. Independent final reviewer was unavailable due provider errors.

A subsequent user drought run failed validation after one round; its ten finalized turns were retained and unfinished drafts discarded. The retained trace does not prove the exact validation cause. GPT-5 reasoning is now disabled for short calls; future validation failures show safe field/type labels without exposing generated input. That failed run was not retried automatically.

## Files

- `misofish/core.py`: schemas, SDK calls, rounds and report validation.
- `misofish/space.py`: authoritative roaming, approach, proximity-weighted encounters and reservations.
- `misofish/server.py`: SQLite, single-job lifecycle, local API.
- `web/`: no-build dashboard, `room.js` shared isometric projection/interpolation/depth sorting, `room.css` room and motion controls.
- `tests/`: no paid requests, local fixture only.
- `requirements.txt`: direct dependencies; `requirements.lock`: tested environment pins.

REA directed source inspection and reuse of existing artifact evidence; see [investigation](MIROFISH-REVERSE-ENGINEERING.md), [new design](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-misofish-design.md) and [plan/verification ledger](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-misofish.md). Saved REA artifact analysis is partial/static, not live execution. No source, prompts, assets or algorithms were copied from `MiroFish/`, and that AGPL-3.0 reference checkout remains separate and untouched. This statement is not licensing advice.

For this upgrade, REA routes the full source checkout to source tools. Tracing confirmed MiroFish concurrently steps platform environments and polls completed action records; its focused UI uses letter avatars, not streamed human figures. OASIS within-step ordering is unknown. Our explicit paired dependencies, genuine SSE text and 2.5D renderer are independent design choices: [upgrade design](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-conversation-room-design.md), [plan](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-conversation-room.md).

The [open-room correction](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-open-room.md) replaces the earlier paired-card design and rotating scheduler. **43 tests passed twice.** Browser verification: one shared floor, ten sprites, zero pair cards, over 1,000 changing position sets, up to four simultaneous live speakers, no page errors. Layout fits 375/768/1440px; motion pause and reduced motion work. Independent review prompted cancellation-at-commit, stale recovery, foot-anchor, bubble overlap and pause fixes. Saved election actions remain intact; no new paid Azure run was started for this correction.

# Open-room correction

User correction: pair cards are not a shared 2.5D room; people should wander and discuss with anyone dynamically. Continuing prior explicit build-with-defaults approval; no additional preference interview.

## Accepted direction
One shared isometric room, upright local SVG people projected onto one floor, depth sorting, extruded walls/floor/props, continuous movement interpolation. No separate conversation cards or permanent partners. Backend owns world positions and encounter reservations; browser renders the same state rather than decorative random motion unrelated to conversation. Preserve live SDK/SSE, ten-agent cap, one spoken turn per agent per cycle, sequential dependent response, max four independent encounters, saved runs/summary/cancel and cost ceiling. Movement/encounter selection uses standard-library randomness, not extra LLM calls. Random proximity-driven selection is a heuristic, not autonomous model-controlled navigation.

## Implementation
- [ ] RED: spatial engine tests for seeded bounded roaming, nearby encounter selection, disjoint reservations and changing contacts; conversation dependency/concurrency tests preserved.
- [ ] GREEN: add misofish/space.py Room; run_round chooses encounter as actors become available; roaming continues for free actors while other streams run; approach/speaking/listening/release events. No upfront pairing list. Injectable RNG/pacing for fast repeatable tests; production movement pacing enabled.
- [ ] GREEN: persist room snapshots from room_state events, restore on reconnect; save action positions for recorded replay. Old saved runs get a layout only, do not claim historic motion/pairing evidence.
- [ ] RED/GREEN UI: one scene with floor/walls/depth-sorted sprites, interpolated motion and anchored bubbles; selected speaker full text; pause visual motion, reduced-motion support; transcript remains accessible. Remove old lane view/code, update wording and README.
- [ ] VERIFY: full tests, browser fixture observes room movement and real partial dialogue, old-run compatibility, one shared floor/no lane cards, depth sorting, no page overflow 375/768/1440, safe text, reconnect and stopped animation on hidden views. No new paid run.

## Constraints
No key changes, new dependencies, source copying, commits or modifying MiroFish. Outer folder is not a Git repo. TDD tests must still guard exact reply parent, cap/cost, cancel, concurrency and preservation. No broad rewrites outside room/scheduler needed.

## Ledger
Plan/design scoped to user-requested correction. Existing source inspected: fixed rotating pairs were created in core.run_round and independently duplicated in room.render. Both are removed; correcting only layout would hide rather than solve the issue.

## Implementation and verification
- Room provides seeded bounded wandering, current-proximity weighted contact selection, reservations/approach/speaking/listening/release. Scheduler creates encounters at runtime as resources free; no upfront pairing list. Backend events/checkpoints feed renderer, finalized turns retain positions.
- Renderer is one shared extruded isometric floor/walls/props, projected upright/depth-sorted people, eased movement, speech anchored to actual speaker, selected full speech and motion control. Pair-card layout/styles removed. Old saved runs show layout only, never claimed historical motion.
- Spatial tests failed before missing module implementation then passed. Two old fixed-ID assumptions replaced by causal/non-self assertions. Fresh reviewer found cancellation between stop check and commit lock, stale room event on recovery, label-dependent foot anchor, collision placement and incomplete pause; regressions/fixes applied. Browser caught selected variable shadowing person constructor; renamed and verified.
- Browser fixture: 1193 render samples / 1145 distinct position sets, max four live speakers/bubbles, no page errors; one room/ten figures/no pair cards. Overflow checks 375/768/1440 match viewport; paused class/reduced motion none; saved runs intact.
- Repeated tests exposed fast pending future error swallowed when another successful future was collected before coordinator stop. Deterministic regression observed fail, now every pending future is collected and incomplete non-cancelled cycles cannot yield successful report. Functional test completion wait bounded at 10s, cleanup requests cancellation and verifies worker exit before DB removal. No production validation weakened.
- Final full suite twice: 43 tests OK (7.8s / 6.4s), JS syntax and pip checks clean, diagnostics no errors. No paid Azure run, key edits, new dependencies, commits or reference source copying for this correction.
- Deliberate bounds: random proximity heuristic, max ten people/four streams, once-per-person-per-cycle speech budget; not LLM navigation or large crowd/pathfinding simulation.

toolSpecificData.result:
**Findings**
At the requested revision, MiroFish is materially more than a three-field persona plus a short transcript, but it does **not** implement a default population of 10 adjustable personas. Preparation creates one profile per selected graph entity; the adjustable `parallel_profile_count` controls generation concurrency, not population size. The API defaults that worker count to 5, while the service method defaults to 3. See [simulation preparation API](MiroFish/backend/app/api/simulation.py#L390), [manager](MiroFish/backend/app/services/simulation_manager.py#L244), and [profile generation](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L927).

**Reconstructed Path**
- **Ontology to graph:** The ontology prompt requests exactly 10 entity types, including eight scenario-specific types and fallback `Person` and `Organization`, plus 6–10 relationship types ([ontology prompt](MiroFish/backend/app/services/ontology_generator.py#L113)). Validation normalizes names, attributes, and endpoints; it adds missing fallbacks and caps the list at 10, but does not enforce exactly 10 or move already-present fallbacks to the last two positions ([validator](MiroFish/backend/app/services/ontology_generator.py#L432)). The graph builder turns definitions into typed Zep entity/edge schemas and installs valid edge endpoints ([graph builder](MiroFish/backend/app/services/graph_builder.py#L313)). Document text is ingested separately in batches, so the ontology is a schema for extraction, not the graph content itself ([graph builder](MiroFish/backend/app/services/graph_builder.py#L413)).
- **Entity selection and enrichment:** Node/edge reads use cursor pagination at 100 items per page, with no default total-item cap ([paging helper](MiroFish/backend/app/utils/zep_paging.py#L121)). The reader selects nodes bearing at least one label besides `Entity` and `Node`; when `defined_entity_types` is supplied, a label must match it exactly. It uses the first matching custom label as the selected type ([entity reader](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_entity_reader.py#L221)). For each selected entity it attaches all matching incoming and outgoing edges, their facts, and basic linked-node data: UUID, name, labels, and summary ([entity reader](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_entity_reader.py#L290)). This is graph adjacency, not a recent-message window.
- **Profile context and generation:** Context combines entity attributes, the full locally attached adjacency, and separate Zep semantic searches by entity name: up to 30 edges and 20 nodes with `rrf` reranking. Results are deduplicated; the assembled context includes at most 15 retrieved facts and 10 node summaries, and each persona prompt receives at most 3,000 characters ([profile enrichment](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L348), [context assembly](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L457), [prompt context limit](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L721)). The profile record includes identity, `bio`, detailed `persona`, platform statistics, age, gender, MBTI, country, profession, topics, and source entity UUID/type ([profile schema](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L65)).
- **What is generated versus enforced:** The prompts ask for detailed individual or institutional personas, including history, relationships, event involvement, behavior, attitudes, and “personal/institutional memory” ([individual prompt](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L721), [group prompt](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L770)). Those are model-generated narrative, not verified facts or enforced behavior. Classification is also a fixed list check: listed individual types get the individual prompt; all other types fall through to the group prompt. A generated type such as `Professor` is not in the individual list. The model gets up to three JSON-generation attempts, then rule-based fallback; batch-level exceptions produce a basic profile ([profile generation and fallback](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L540), [individual-type list](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L232)).
- **Relationship boundary:** Graph relationships inform persona context, but MiroFish does not explicitly pass source graph edges as seeded OASIS follow ties. Platform serializers omit `source_entity_uuid` and `source_entity_type`; the runner passes the Twitter CSV or Reddit JSON profile path to the OASIS agent-graph generator ([Twitter export](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L1114), [Reddit export](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L1190), [Twitter initialization](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1133), [Reddit initialization](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1324)). The inspected MiroFish path therefore establishes relationships as generated context, not as initialized social-graph edges. External OASIS internals were not inspected.
- **Platform profile contract:** Twitter exports `user_id`, name, username, `user_char` (bio plus persona), and description; Reddit exports persona and additional profile fields. These adapters preserve more than three fields, though platform outputs differ ([Twitter serializer](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L1114), [Reddit serializer](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L1190)).
- **Simulation memory updates:** The runner tails platform `actions.jsonl` and forwards action records to the updater ([simulation runner](MiroFish/backend/app/services/simulation_runner.py#L790)). The updater skips event records, failed actions, and `DO_NOTHING`; it converts successful actions into timestamped natural-language episode text ([updater](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_graph_memory_updater.py#L36), [action filtering](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_graph_memory_updater.py#L383)). It batches five activities per platform, bounds episode text, then appends a text episode to the graph with simulation/platform/round/agent/action metadata ([batching](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_graph_memory_updater.py#L228), [episode write](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_graph_memory_updater.py#L494)). This is an append-and-extract workflow, not a direct edge mutation or a write keyed to the original entity UUID. Shutdown waits for returned episode UUIDs to become processed and surfaces failed or timed-out ingestion ([ingestion barrier](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_graph_memory_updater.py#L599)). Existing tests cover provenance, failed-action filtering, queue draining, and the wait deadline ([updater tests](MiroFish/backend/tests/test_zep_graph_memory_updater.py#L50), [provenance test](MiroFish/backend/tests/test_zep_graph_memory_updater.py#L86), [failed-action test](MiroFish/backend/tests/test_zep_graph_memory_updater.py#L123)).
- **Report retrieval is separate:** `quick_search` performs Zep edge search; `insight_forge` generates subqueries and retrieves edges/endpoints; `panorama_search` reads all nodes and edges and classifies temporal/historical facts ([Zep tools](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_tools.py#L457), [InsightForge](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_tools.py#L943), [Panorama](MiroFish/backend/app/services/zep_tools.py#L1143)). These are report-time retrieval tools, not the simulation memory writer.

**Reusable Principles**
Keep ontology/schema construction, graph-backed entity selection, profile generation, platform adaptation, and simulation memory ingestion as distinct stages. Preserve entity provenance across them; combine explicit adjacency with bounded relevance retrieval; treat model-written persona claims as generated rather than observed; separate requested persona count from worker concurrency; and make appended simulation episodes traceable and ingestion-confirmed. These principles capture the architecture without copying its source.

**Acceptance Checks**
1. With at least 10 eligible entities, preparation creates 10 personas by default; a separate user setting changes that count without changing generation concurrency.
2. When fewer than the requested count are eligible, the result reports the shortfall rather than silently fabricating people.
3. Entity selection honors custom labels and optional type filters; graph reads handle multiple cursor pages.
4. Each selected profile receives inbound and outbound relationship facts and linked-node context.
5. Profile output has a defined, tested schema and platform mapping; unknown or unsupported biographical details remain distinguishable from source-grounded data.
6. The entity-to-profile mapping is preserved, and graph relationships are either deliberately seeded as social ties or explicitly documented as context-only.
7. Only successful, meaningful actions become timestamped memory episodes with simulation provenance; failed writes and pending ingestion are surfaced.
8. A simulation-generated episode can be found by subsequent graph retrieval, without treating report search as the write mechanism.

**Open Questions**
The reference provides no persona-count selection or sampling policy; that needs a reconstruction decision, including behavior when there are more eligible entities than the requested count. It also leaves unresolved whether graph edges should become actual initial social ties, how generated biographical claims should carry evidence/provenance, and whether later persona generation should consume simulation episodes. I inspected relevant tests but did not run them; this was read-only source research.

toolSpecificData.result:
**Finding**

This is not a random pair/proximity interaction engine, but its active-agent scheduler is random. MiroFish selects actors independently of the social graph, then delegates each selected actor’s decision to OASIS/CAMEL. OASIS provides real feeds, action tools, SQLite-backed social state, and recommendation algorithms, but that richer behavior does not make actor selection graph-driven.

### Actual step

For each platform, MiroFish computes a simulated hour from the round number, applies peak/off-peak multipliers, filters agents by `active_hours`, samples each candidate by `activity_level`, then randomly samples up to the target count. The setting names say “per hour,” but the selection happens once per round. `round_num` is passed to the selector but does not affect its selection. The current defaults in the selector are 5–20; configuration can override them. There is no seed in this script.

Each selected agent is mapped to `LLMAction()` and submitted in one `env.step`. The harness skips `env.step` entirely when no actors are selected. The local anchors are [the actor selector](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1040), [platform setup and simulation loop](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1155), and [round configuration](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1551).

The OASIS call path, as surfaced in source search, is:

1. `env.step` updates the recommendation table, builds tasks for the supplied actions, and gathers them concurrently. LLM work is gated by the environment semaphore; MiroFish sets it to 30. The platform receives action requests through a channel and processes them in its `running` loop. Relevant source paths: [OASIS env.py, step](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/environment/env.py#L140), [env.py, task execution and clock](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/environment/env.py#L188), [platform.py, request loop](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L128).
2. For `LLMAction`, OASIS calls the agent’s LLM action method. The agent refreshes its environment observation, builds a user prompt around it, and calls `astep`; available social functions are exposed as tools and filtered by the supplied action list. [agent.py, constructor](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent.py#L70), [agent.py, LLM action](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent.py#L125), [agent_action.py, social tool methods](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent_action.py#L23).
3. Tool calls mutate the platform database. Posts, comments, follows and interaction traces are recorded in SQLite; for example, [platform.py, create_post](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L400), [platform.py, follow](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L859), and [platform.py, create_comment](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L1079).
4. After `env.step` returns, MiroFish reads new `trace` rows and writes selected action details to JSONL. It filters `refresh` and `sign_up` from that log, not from the SQLite state. [action extraction and trace enrichment](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L657).

Thus, agents within a platform step reason concurrently; their platform requests can arrive in completion-dependent order and are then handled by the platform loop. Twitter and Reddit simulations are also launched with `asyncio.gather`. There is no seeded reproducibility in the harness, and OASIS refresh/recommendation code also uses randomness.

### Observation, memory, and social behavior

An agent’s decision prompt is based on its profile plus a refreshed feed. The OASIS environment obtains posts through `refresh`; those results include post content and comments. [agent_environment.py, posts](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent_environment.py#L54). Twitter refresh can add posts from followed accounts, ranked by likes; [platform.py, refresh](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L258). Reddit’s default recommendation algorithm uses hot-score ranking; [recsys.py, Reddit recommendations](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/recsys.py#L214). The trace-personalized recommendation implementation uses prior like/dislike traces and content similarity; [recsys.py, trace-personalized ranking](https://github.com/camel-ai/oasis/blob/v0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/recsys.py#L689).

These are OASIS defaults, not MiroFish’s generated platform weights. The runner calls `oasis.make` with the default platform type and database path; it does not pass MiroFish’s `recency_weight`, `popularity_weight`, `relevance_weight`, `viral_threshold`, or `echo_chamber_strength`. Those are generated configuration, not enforcement. The config generator is at [simulation_config_generator.py](MiroFish/backend/app/services/simulation_config_generator.py).

There is a per-agent `SocialAgent` object reused across rounds and the OASIS path calls `astep` without resetting that object. CAMEL’s `ChatAgent` normally supplies the conversational memory behind that call. However, I could not inspect the exact `camel-ai==0.2.78` archive here, so its exact memory implementation and retention policy remain **unverified against the pin**. The harness does not itself persist or restore CAMEL conversation memory between processes. MiroFish’s optional Zep action-memory ingestion is a separate synchronization path, not something this runner supplies to each `LLMAction` prompt.

The configured action sets materially narrow behavior: Twitter allows create-post, like, repost, follow, do-nothing and quote; Reddit allows posts, comments, likes/dislikes, search, trend, refresh, follow, mute and do-nothing. Therefore normal Twitter agents here do not have comment or group-message tools, and Reddit agents do not have group-message tools. OASIS has group-chat actions, but this runner does not enable them. There is no enabled point-to-point direct conversation action: interaction is through posts, comments, quotes/reposts and other enabled actions. Interviews are manual IPC actions, not agent-to-agent conversation.

### Provenance and limitation

The workspace and searched package-cache locations contained no matching dependency archives, and `.rea/reference-packages` does not exist. PyPI’s release metadata gives these archive URLs and published SHA256 values:

| Pin | Archive | Published SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| `camel-oasis==0.2.5` | [sdist](https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/d9/6f/b36240380c65397f3e18829fce8ed0a1d19893b32d3596aa0902c7b3ad81/camel_oasis-0.2.5.tar.gz) | `f667dc86f9f7823d50f76b07733a34afc1427b923f1a673519206bb41a57f8c` |
| `camel-oasis==0.2.5` | [wheel](https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/77/d0/6d6173602433937d0228b7809e2b244e09c11cfb1be9c6754ae3b20d887/camel_oasis-0.2.5-py3-none-any.whl) | `9ebd6ba8e331495ee56b25cc63982188b94125de499e5e9c00398a1d47e606d` |
| `camel-ai==0.2.78` | [sdist](https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/3b/2b/cd5181fd0ebcf567a088ee5c1e3768b132ba4b1489ee19d5fb0bd679586/camel_ai-0.2.78.tar.gz) | `24745da225da7da96dcd85f72143c6104569c17f14280c369d7e82b86851284` |
| `camel-ai==0.2.78` | [wheel](https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/01/81/0cfb1c0d9da589665e2eb4418879670e70bba428638c37fb4f6a78baf300/camel_ai-0.2.78-py3-none-any.whl) | `356624da13dfe0c55ef43dc509c18ce029f67fe3997966495a4ce9be31078d5` |

These are PyPI-published digests, not hashes independently computed from downloaded files. I could verify the OASIS `v0.2.5` rendered source paths, but this session has no download-command tool; the rendered-source fetcher also failed to return file bodies. So the archives were **not downloaded or unpacked**, and the internal behavior above is not fully verified against the exact wheel contents. No source was executed, no LLM/cloud was called, and no application files were changed.

### Reconstruction acceptance checks

1. Default actor count is exactly 10 per configured time unit; an explicit override is honored, validated, and capped to available eligible agents.
2. Actor activation is driven by agent schedules, activity state, events and network context, not random pair/proximity sampling.
3. Given a fixed seed and deterministic model stub, actor selection, action ordering and platform state are reproducible.
4. Each active-agent decision receives a documented observation snapshot; tests prove what posts/comments are visible and how follow/mute/reply relationships filter or rank them.
5. A complete step verifies action-tool selection and persisted effects across posts, comments, follows and trace records.
6. Per-agent memory is retained across steps, scoped by agent, and its persistence/reset behavior is explicitly tested.
7. No-agent rounds have explicit clock semantics; MiroFish’s round-derived hour must not silently diverge from OASIS platform time.
8. If direct conversations are required, a test demonstrates the supported conversation mechanism and its persisted messages; posts/comments alone do not satisfy it.

toolSpecificData.result:
**Run-specific evidence**
`data/runs.db` exists, but I could not query SQLite with the available read-only tools; a text search cannot inspect its binary contents. So I could not verify this run’s event tail, action kinds, reply IDs, or persisted error. I won’t infer the cause from “failed, round 2, 22 actions.”

The source does show why the saved error won’t identify a `ValueError`: the manager maps all such exceptions to “Invalid or incomplete model output,” and the terminal event persists that sanitized message ([server.py](misofish/server.py#L247), [server.py](misofish/server.py#L259)). Several distinct failures can reach that handler, including invalid reply targets, incomplete cycles, and invalid report citations ([core.py](misofish/core.py#L249), [server.py](misofish/server.py#L211), [core.py](misofish/core.py#L316)). Exact cause remains **unknown**.

**Cheapest diagnostic regression**
Extend the existing FakeModel failure test in [test_events.py](tests/test_events.py#L27): have the fake return a schema-valid reply to the wrong completed parent, then assert the saved error has a stable, allowlisted code and phase, plus safe turn/reply IDs. Preserve its existing assertions that the parent action remains saved and the draft is cleared. The current test exercises a `ValueError` but does not check a useful persisted diagnosis. Do not persist exception text or model output; distinguish cases with codes such as `reply_target_mismatch` or `report_citation_invalid`.

**Pacing and display boundary**
Live dialogue is genuinely streamed over SSE and rendered on each update ([app.js](web/app.js#L203), [app.js](web/app.js#L210)). The scheduler runs up to four encounters concurrently, with each pair’s turns sequential ([core.py](misofish/core.py#L221)). The `1.4s` timer is only for saved-conversation replay; “Pause visual motion” does not pause generation or replay ([app.js](web/app.js#L280), [app.js](web/app.js#L303)). Room bubbles truncate text to 170 characters, with the transcript/selected-speech view providing the fuller reading surface ([room.js](web/room.js#L134), [room.js](web/room.js#L141)).

I’d keep live generation real-time and address “too fast” at the viewing layer: give recorded playback pause, step, and speed controls, and keep complete turns easy to read in the transcript. If replay should reflect original timing, the event log needs timestamps; its current cursor is ordered by event ID, not recorded time ([server.py](misofish/server.py#L46)).

**Graph/persona ownership**
In this app, personas are generated from scenario/source text and a requested count; there is no graph input to persona preparation ([core.py](misofish/core.py#L173)). Contact choice is separately driven by seeded random movement and nearby-coordinate weighting, with a weak repeat-contact penalty ([space.py](misofish/space.py#L40), [space.py](misofish/space.py#L73)). That makes proximity a visual/scheduling heuristic, not a semantic or social relationship.

In the MiroFish reference, `GraphPanel` renders and inspects graph nodes and edges, while `Step3Simulation` presents platform activity timelines. The workflow owner for graph-backed persona preparation is Step 2: `SimulationView` composes `GraphPanel` with `Step2EnvSetup` ([SimulationView.vue](MiroFish/MiroFish/frontend/src/views/SimulationView.vue#L42), [SimulationView.vue](MiroFish/MiroFish/frontend/src/views/SimulationView.vue#L53), [Step2EnvSetup.vue](MiroFish/MiroFish/frontend/src/components/Step2EnvSetup.vue#L45)). So `GraphPanel` is a useful graph-inspection reference, not the persona-generation owner; Step 3 is not the right place to decide graph-grounded identity or relationships.

For a mature redesign, make explicit, evidence-linked persona relationships drive interaction selection; keep room coordinates as layout only. Do not treat a domain knowledge-graph edge as a human social tie without evidence. Preserve old runs as legacy snapshots: retain action/event IDs and reports, don’t infer historical graph edges or encounter reasons, and don’t replay generation. New graph/provenance fields should be optional and versioned so old runs still load.

No files were edited, no tests were run, and no paid or cloud requests were made. To finish the run-specific check, this read-only snippet prints only safe snapshot fields and an allowlisted event tail; it omits scenario/source, persona text, turn text, and report content:

```python
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import sqlite3

run_id = "bba6089ecb6f4505a8f61eaca7d686b6"
db = sqlite3.connect("file:data/runs.db?mode=ro", uri=True)
db.execute("PRAGMA query_only=ON")

row = db.execute("SELECT snapshot FROM runs WHERE id=?", (run_id,)).fetchone()
if row is None:
    raise SystemExit("Run not found")

run = json.loads(row[0])
action_keys = ("id", "round", "agent_id", "kind", "partner_id", "lane", "reply_to", "encounter_id")
print(json.dumps({
    "id": run.get("id"),
    "status": run.get("status"),
    "round": run.get("round"),
    "model": run.get("model"),
    "agent_count": run.get("config", {}).get("agent_count"),
    "requested_rounds": run.get("config", {}).get("rounds"),
    "error": run.get("error"),
    "actions": [{k: a.get(k) for k in action_keys} for a in run.get("actions", [])],
}, indent=2))

rows = db.execute(
    "SELECT id,kind,payload FROM events WHERE run_id=? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 16",
    (run_id,),
).fetchall()
safe_keys = ("turn_id", "agent_id", "partner_id", "round", "lane", "reply_to", "status", "error")
for event_id, kind, payload in reversed(rows):
    data = json.loads(payload)
    safe = {k: data[k] for k in safe_keys if k in data}
    if kind == "turn_complete" and isinstance(data.get("action"), dict):
        action = data["action"]
        safe["action"] = {k: action.get(k) for k in action_keys}
    print(json.dumps({"event_id": event_id, "kind": kind, "data": safe}))
PY
```

toolSpecificData.result:
**Reference identity**  
I treated the unpacked trees as the requested references: OASIS `camel-oasis 0.2.5` (SHA-256 supplied: `9ebd6ba8e331495ee56b25cc63982188b94125dde499e5e9c00398a1d47e606d`) and CAMEL `0.2.78` (supplied: `356624da13dfe0c55ef43dc509c18ce029f67fe3997966495a4ce9be931078d5`). This was static source inspection only.

**Decision to effects**
- MiroFish selects agents using `active_hours` and `activity_level`, then creates one `LLMAction` per active agent and calls `env.step()`. Its round duration determines scheduling and total rounds; it does not directly set OASIS’s platform clock. [run_parallel_simulation.py](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1040) [run_parallel_simulation.py](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1216) [run_parallel_simulation.py](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1253)
- OASIS updates the recommendation table first, then schedules each manual or LLM action and awaits them with `asyncio.gather`; Twitter advances `time_step` once after the batch completes. MiroFish sets the LLM semaphore to 30. [env.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/environment/env.py#L136) [env.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/environment/env.py#L152) [env.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/environment/env.py#L193) [run_parallel_simulation.py](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1155)
- Each LLM agent observes posts through `to_text_prompt()`, which calls `refresh()`, then runs CAMEL `astep()`. The resulting social action goes through the channel to the platform’s `running()` consumer, which dispatches to a platform method. The consumer handles queued mutations sequentially. [agent.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent.py#L125) [agent_environment.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent_environment.py#L58) [platform.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L128) [agent_action.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent_action.py#L63)
- MiroFish’s Twitter tool set is `create_post(content)`, `like_post(post_id)`, `repost(post_id)`, `follow(followee_id)`, `do_nothing()`, `quote_post(post_id, quote_content)`. Reddit exposes `like_post(post_id)`, `dislike_post(post_id)`, `create_post(content)`, `create_comment(post_id, content)`, `like_comment(comment_id)`, `dislike_comment(comment_id)`, `search_posts(query)`, `search_user(query)`, `trend()`, `refresh()`, `do_nothing()`, `follow(followee_id)`, `mute(mutee_id)`. These are restricted subsets of OASIS’s function tools; interview is issued as a manual action, not an LLM tool. [run_parallel_simulation.py](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L178) [run_parallel_simulation.py](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L188) [agent_action.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent_action.py#L145) [agent_action.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent_action.py#L192) [agent_action.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent_action.py#L395)
- Effects land in OASIS’s platform database and trace table: for example, `create_post` inserts a post, and `follow` inserts a follow row. `perform_agent_graph_action()` exists, but the LLM path’s call to it is commented out; don’t equate platform follows with updates to the separate in-memory `AgentGraph`. [platform.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L400) [platform.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L859) [agent.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent.py#L150)

**Memory and feeds**
- OASIS `SocialAgent` passes no custom memory or message window to CAMEL. CAMEL defaults to `ChatHistoryMemory`, backed by `InMemoryKeyValueStorage`, with `window_size=None`: history accumulates for the life of that agent instance and is not disk-persistent by default. [agent.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agent.py#L55) [chat_agent.py](.rea/reference-packages/camel-0.2.78/camel/agents/chat_agent.py#L478) [agent_memories.py](.rea/reference-packages/camel-0.2.78/camel/memories/agent_memories.py#L26) [chat_history_block.py](.rea/reference-packages/camel-0.2.78/camel/memories/blocks/chat_history_block.py#L63)
- Storage retention and prompt-context retention differ. Records remain stored, but `ScoreBasedContextCreator` trims the prompt to the model token limit, preferring newer messages; history’s default `keep_rate` is 0.9. `ChatAgent.reset()` calls `init_messages()`, which clears memory and restores the system message. MiroFish reuses agent objects across rounds and keeps the environment alive for interviews, so memory persists across those rounds/interviews, but not across worker-process restarts. [chat_agent.py](.rea/reference-packages/camel-0.2.78/camel/agents/chat_agent.py#L555) [chat_agent.py](.rea/reference-packages/camel-0.2.78/camel/agents/chat_agent.py#L1345) [score_based.py](.rea/reference-packages/camel-0.2.78/camel/memories/context_creators/score_based.py#L65) [chat_history_block.py](.rea/reference-packages/camel-0.2.78/camel/memories/blocks/chat_history_block.py#L59) [run_parallel_simulation.py](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1281)
- Twitter’s default OASIS platform uses `twhin-bert`, with 2 recommendation posts, a buffer of 2, and up to 3 followed-user posts. Reddit uses its own hot-score recommender, with a 5-post refresh and buffer of 100. The feed refresh selects followed users’ posts by descending likes, but then deduplicates and queries with `IN` and no `ORDER BY`; the final observed order is not guaranteed to preserve that ranking. [env.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/environment/env.py#L81) [env.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/environment/env.py#L92) [platform.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L258) [platform.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L304)
- The Twitter recommender uses profile/bio text and recent-post text embeddings, weighted by recency; interaction-based like scoring is off by default. MiroFish’s configured recency/popularity/relevance weights, viral threshold, and echo-chamber strength are generated into config but are not passed into `oasis.make()` or applied by the runner. The runner does consume time and agent activity settings for round scheduling. [recsys.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/recsys.py#L419) [simulation_config_generator.py](MiroFish/backend/app/services/simulation_config_generator.py#L343) [run_parallel_simulation.py](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1155) [run_parallel_simulation.py](MiroFish/backend/scripts/run_parallel_simulation.py#L1068)
- Twitter’s platform clock defaults to `Clock(60)` and advances by OASIS `env.step()` calls, not MiroFish’s simulated minutes. Reddit timestamps instead use scaled wall-clock time. [platform.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/platform.py#L77) [clock.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/clock/clock.py#L18) [env.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/environment/env.py#L198)

**Graphs and profiles**
- MiroFish reads Zep entities with `enrich_with_edges=True`; those related facts/nodes enrich the generated persona. They are not automatically OASIS follow edges. [simulation_manager.py](MiroFish/backend/app/services/simulation_manager.py#L299) [simulation_manager.py](MiroFish/backend/app/services/simulation_manager.py#L357)
- In this code, the Zep/document graph supplies source entities and contextual facts; OASIS `AgentGraph` is a separate directed social graph of agents and `FOLLOW` edges. MiroFish exports Twitter identity/persona columns and Reddit profile fields, but no follow list. The OASIS generators MiroFish actually calls create empty `nodes`/`edges` and add agents without seeding follows. [oasis_profile_generator.py](MiroFish/backend/app/services/oasis_profile_generator.py#L1114) [agents_generator.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agents_generator.py#L567) [agents_generator.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agents_generator.py#L614)
- Correction: OASIS has a different CSV-generation path that reads `following_agentid_list`, seeds graph edges, and inserts prior posts; MiroFish does not call that path. [agents_generator.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agents_generator.py#L120) [agents_generator.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_agent/agents_generator.py#L128)

**Compatibility and recommendation**
OASIS metadata requires Python `>=3.10,<3.12`; CAMEL `0.2.78` requires `>=3.10,<3.13`, so their compatible intersection is Python 3.10 or 3.11. OASIS pins CAMEL, igraph, pandas, and sentence-transformers versions. Its default Twitter path also lazily loads `Twitter/twhin-bert-base` and selects CUDA if available, otherwise CPU; model availability/download and CPU inference are practical startup/resource considerations beyond the metadata’s Python constraint. [OASIS METADATA](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/camel_oasis-0.2.5.dist-info/METADATA#L11) [CAMEL METADATA](.rea/reference-packages/camel-0.2.78/camel_ai-0.2.78.dist-info/METADATA#L12) [recsys.py](.rea/reference-packages/oasis-0.2.5/oasis/social_platform/recsys.py#L69)

**Recommendation:** Keep the real OASIS engine in an isolated worker if the goal is behavioral fidelity: it already supplies concurrent agent decisions, platform effects, feed construction, traces, and per-agent CAMEL memory. Treat MiroFish’s platform recommendation weights and social-tie seeding as currently unimplemented inputs; translate them into OASIS platform settings and explicit follow rows if they’re required. An independent graph/memory room would be simpler to control, but would diverge from OASIS’s action, feed, timing, and token-pruning semantics.

response.value: The graph has two distinct roles in MiroFish: source facts inform personas, while OASIS maintains social state such as follows, posts, comments, and feeds. They are not automatically the same graph. The redesign needs to preserve that distinction and expose why an agent saw a message or chose an interaction, rather than implying a relationship from room placement.

response.value: The pinned source confirms persistent per-agent memory across rounds, feed observations, tool-driven actions, and stored social state. I recommend using the real OASIS/CAMEL engine instead of inventing another scheduler; the main choice is whether to retain MiroFish’s Zep Cloud graph or build a local graph alternative. I’ll document the design and that tradeoff for approval.
